title: Architectural Drift: A Post-Mortem on Context Deficit and Token Over-Reliance in Multi-Turn LLM Alignment
summary: This paper examines the operational breakdown of large language models (LLMs) during extended, multi-turn technical collaborations. Specifically, we analyze the engineering flaws that cause an agent to repeatedly execute deprecated instructions (e.g., generating programmatic payloads after explicit user prohibition). We demonstrate that this failure mode is not a conscious refusal, but a structural consequence of attention-weight dilution, recency bias in the context window, and pattern-matching traps induced by automated system templates.

review.reason: Analysis of context loss and instruction drift in multi-turn LLM collaborations.
